title: Senior's toolkit: tests, wiring and shipping
summary: dotnet test options, DI registration, options and secrets, benchmarking, and packing a .NET tool.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: tests, wiring and shipping
steps.body: Advanced C# at work is mostly plumbing: running the right tests, wiring services with the right lifetime, keeping secrets out of git, proving a speed-up with numbers, and shipping a tool. These are the commands and APIs for each.

toolkit.what: Run the test projects. A few options turn a slow, opaque run into a fast, informative one.
flags: only matching tests (`~` contains, `=` exact, `Category=Slow` for a trait)
every test's name, result and output
if a test hangs for 2 minutes, dump the process and name the test
write a Cobertura coverage file (needs the coverlet.collector package)

toolkit.what: Register a service with Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection. The lifetime decides how long one instance lives, and getting it wrong is a real production bug.
flags: one instance for the whole app: must be thread-safe
one per request in ASP.NET Core: the usual choice for a DbContext
a new instance every time it is asked for
a singleton must never hold a scoped service

toolkit.what: Bind a configuration section to a class, check it, and fail at start-up instead of on the first email. Services receive it as `IOptions<SmtpOptions>`.
flags: read the `Smtp` section of appsettings, environment variables and secrets
throw at start-up if it is invalid
when the value can change while the app runs

toolkit.what: Keep development passwords and API keys out of the repository. They are stored in your user profile and read like appsettings, in the Development environment.
flags: add a UserSecretsId to the project (once)
which project, when you are not in its folder

toolkit.what: Measure a speed-up properly: warm-up, many iterations, statistics and allocations. A `Stopwatch` around one call is not evidence.
flags: the version the others are compared to (Ratio column)
add the Allocated column: bytes per call
run each benchmark for several input sizes
benchmarks must run in Release; it refuses Debug

toolkit.what: Build a NuGet package. With `<PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>` in the project, the package is a .NET tool that anyone can install as a command.
Install a .NET tool, from nuget.org or from a local folder of packages.
flags: also look in this folder for the package
the same options, to move to a newer version
pin it in the repo's tool manifest, restored with `dotnet tool restore`

steps.prompt: The CI job has been "running tests" for 5 hours with no output and is finally killed. Locally all tests pass. What do you add to the `dotnet test` command so the next run tells you which test hangs?
options: `--blame-hang-timeout 5m`, which dumps the process and names the test that was running when it hung
steps.explain: Blame mode records which tests started and did not finish, and with a hang timeout it takes a dump and stops the run. A hang that only happens in CI is often a deadlock (`.Result` with a sync context) or a test waiting on a network resource.

steps.prompt: The app refuses to start in Development with this message. What is wrong?
steps.code: System.InvalidOperationException: Cannot consume scoped service 'Shop.Data.AppDbContext' from singleton 'Shop.Reports.ReportCache'.
options: `ReportCache` is a singleton that takes an `AppDbContext`, so one DbContext would live forever and be shared by every request; make the cache create a scope (`IServiceScopeFactory`) or change its lifetime
`AppDbContext` needs to be registered as a singleton too
steps.explain: This is the captive dependency check, on by default in Development. Making the DbContext a singleton would "fix" the message and create a thread-safety bug. Keep the DbContext scoped and let the singleton create a scope when it needs one.

steps.prompt: Match each lifetime or option to its meaning.
pairs: one instance for the whole app

steps.prompt: Put the steps of shipping `sk` as a .NET tool and installing it locally in order.
Store the development API key outside the repository.
steps.explain: `set` stores the value, and `:` separates configuration sections, so it binds to `Weather.ApiKey`. (In environment variables the separator is `__`, because `:` is not allowed everywhere.)

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Rerun only the failing tests with `--filter`, and give CI a `--blame-hang-timeout` so a hang tells you its name. Think about the lifetime every time you register a service, validate options at start-up, and never put a secret in appsettings.json. Show a BenchmarkDotNet table before you claim a speed-up in review.
